body: Thanks for reporting.  It seems like the connection has been closed before all pending messages were handled.

@trustin @fbettag yeah.. I think what we need to do is to make sure we fail-fast if someone tries to flush after the connection was closed. Otherwise we may crash the JVM if one of the buffers is direct and we freed it before. WDYT ?
@normanmaurer It's not really related with the `flush()` operation in Netty. :-)  I'll take care of it anyway.

`inboundBufferUpdated()` should not be invoked at all after an inbound buffer has been freed.  However, the pasted stack trace tells us that, for an unknown reason, `inboundBufferUpdated()` was invoked after `freeInboundBuffer()`.

Another weird thing is that the `MessageBridge` object of the context is not null.  Because the handler is running on an I/O thread, the `MessageBridge` should be null and thus `MessageBridge.flush()` should not be called at all.

What dynamic changes did you make on a pipeline, @fbettag ?

@trustin: We only use the ProtoNegoHandler from the PortUnification Example. Nothing else modifies the Pipeline!
